questions.question: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Yesterday was the worse day of my life.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.
Yesterday was the worse day of my life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. worst .

Key Points

  • The given sentence talks about a particular day in the past that was extremely bad, hence it requires the superlative form of the adjective.
  • The word "worse" is the comparative form of "bad," while "worst" is the superlative form.
  • Since the sentence states that it was the single most bad day, the correct word to use is "worst".

Correct sentence: Yesterday was the worst day of my life.

Additional Information

  • Comparative and Superlative Forms:
    • Comparative: Used to compare two things. Example: "better" is the comparative form of "good."
    • Superlative: Used to describe the highest degree of something among three or more things. Example: "best" is the superlative form of "good."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. Rashmi is not only smart but very beautiful.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

Rashmi is not only smart but very beautiful.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is but also very beautiful

Key Points

  • The conjunction pair is not only...but also.
  • Correlative conjunctions always come in pairs and they relate one part of the sentence to the other. "Not only... but also" can be used to connect either nouns or clauses. 

Additional Information

  • Using not only . . . but also in a sentence, parallelism should be the goal. It means that the words following both parts of this correlative conjunction (i.e., not only and but also) should belong to the same parts of speech. For example, if a verb follows not only, then a verb should also follow but also. Using different parts of speech after each part of not only . . . but also makes the sentence imbalanced and, frankly, just awkward. 
    Example: He’s not only intelligent but also has a great sense of humor.
                     He’s not only intelligent but also funny.
     

Thus the correct sentence will be: Rashmi is not only smart but also very beautiful.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. Sunil have been working as a personal assistant to the Director for two years.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.

Sunil have been working as a personal assistant to the Director for two years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'has been working.'

Key Points

  • In the underlined segment, the plural form of the verb ''have'' is incorrect.
  • The subject 'Sunil' in the given sentence is a singular subject.
  • The singular form of the verb 'has' should be used with the singular subject 'Sunil'.
  • Therefore, the singular form of the verb ''has'' should be used in place of the plural form 'have'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: Sunil has been working as a personal assistant to the Director for two years.

Additional Information

  • Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural). (विषय और क्रिया एक दूसरे के साथ संख्या (एकवचन या बहुवचन) में सहमत होना चाहिए)
  • Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if the subject is plural, its verb must also be plural. (इस प्रकार, यदि कोई विषय एकवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी एकवचन होनी चाहिए ; यदि विषय बहुवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी बहुवचन होनी चाहिए)
     

Hinglish

  • रेखांकित खंड में क्रिया 'have' का बहुवचन रूप गलत है ।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में subject 'Sunil' एक एकवचन subject है।
  • क्रिया का एकवचन रूप 'has', एकवचन subject 'Sunil' के साथ प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • इसलिए बहुवचन क्रिया 'have' के स्थान पर एकवचन क्रिया 'has' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

सही वाक्य: Sunil has been working as a personal assistant to the Director for two years.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. You are the beautiful woman I have ever seen.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

You are the beautiful woman I have ever seen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: most beautiful.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the correct superlative form of the adjective should be used.
  • The term 'beautiful' is an adjective that can be modified to its superlative form for comparison.
  • The presence of 'the' before 'beautiful' hints at the fact that the superlative form of 'beautiful' should be used.
  • The correct superlative form of 'beautiful' is 'most beautiful', indicating that no other woman is more beautiful than the one being referred to.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: You are the most beautiful woman I have ever seen.

Additional Information

  • In English grammar, adjectives have three degrees of comparison: positive, comparative, and superlative.
    • Positive degree: describes a single item/person (e.g., beautiful).
    • Comparative degree: compares two items/people (e.g., more beautiful).
    • Superlative degree: compares more than two items/people (e.g., most beautiful).

questions.question: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. Sidharth want to become a football player but needs to practice more rigorously.

Sidharth want to become a football player but needs to practice more rigorously.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - wants to become.

Key Points

  • The simple present tense is used when an action is happening right now, to state or ask about things in general, or when it happens regularly or unceasingly.
  • The structure is given below:
    • Subject + V1 + object.
  • The verb will take 's/es' if the given noun/pronoun (3rd person) is singular.
  • Example:
    • ​He plays badminton daily.​
  • Certain verbs used only in the simple present tense are given below:
    • ​verbs of perception (see, hear, smell, etc.), think, know, has/have, possess, like, want, desire, hate, seem, imagine, etc.
  • Example:
    • ​My brother is owning a car. (incorrect)
    • ​My brother owns a car. (correct)

Correct Sentence: Sidharth wants to become a football player but needs to practice more rigorously.

  • 'Haven't' is the past particle form of the verb used in the interro-negative sense where there is a use and sense 'not' in the sentence (appropriate structure: Have+ not= Haven't).

Thus and so, option 1)

questions.question: Select the option that will substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no substitution is needed, select ‘No substitution required’. When I met the couple yesterday I noticed that the wife was more taller than her husband.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no substitution is needed, select ‘No substitution required’.

When I met the couple yesterday I noticed that the wife was more taller than her husband.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e., 'taller'. 

Key Points

  • The underlined part is grammatically incorrect.
  • Taller is a comparative form of the adjective tall. 
  • We cannot use more before it. 
  • Hence, option 4 is the correct answer. 

Additional Information

  •  For one syllable adjectives 
    • add -er for the comparative and -est for the superlative.
    • If the adjective has a consonant + single vowel + consonant spelling, the final consonant must be doubled before adding the ending.
    • Examples - tall - taller -tallest; big - bigger -biggest
  • For two syllables adjectives
    • ​form the comparative either by adding -er or by preceding the adjective with more.
    • These adjectives form the superlative either by adding -est or by preceding the adjective with most.
    • Examples - happy - happier -happiest; tangled - more tangled - most tangled
  • For three or more syllables adjectives
    • form the comparative by putting more in front of the adjective, and the superlative by putting most in front.
    • Examples - important - more important - most important

Correct sentence: The girl in the water whistled with full might and waved her arms to draw attention to her plight.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Karan was so deep effected by the film that he didn’t speak a word.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Karan was so deep effected by the film that he didn’t speak a word.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'deeply effected'

Key Points

  • The verb in the sentence is the affect that the film has on Karan. so the adverb is deep since it describes the affect.
  • Adverbs usually end with the suffix -ly. So the correct form of the adverb in the sentence should be 'deeply'.
  • The given sentence talks about the impact of the film and affect means impact. So the correct form here should be affected.

Hence, the correct sentence is: Karan was so deeply affected by the film that he didn’t speak a word.

Additional Information

  • Affect is a verb and effect is a noun usually.  Affect stands for action.
  • For example:
    • Lack of sleep affected her performance on the IQ test.
  • Effect is the noun. It can be understood as the result or consequence of a change or action.
  • For example:
    • The cheat meals had an effect on the weight loss program.

Alternate Method

  • An adverb modifies the verb in the sentence
  • Example: She ate her dinner quickly.
  • An adjective modifies the noun in the sentence
    • Example: Anam wore a beautiful gown at the wedding.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'. Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior than her.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior than her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The adjective "junior" is a comparative that is always followed by the preposition "to", not "than".
  • This rule also applies to other similar comparatives like "senior", "inferior", "superior", etc.
  • Using "than" after "junior" is grammatically incorrect in standard English usage.
  • Therefore, the phrase "junior than her" must be corrected to "junior to her".
Hence, the correct answer is Option 1: junior to.
 
Correct Sentence: "Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior to her."
 
Additional Information
  • "Junior to" is the correct grammatical construction when comparing relative rank or age.
  • Examples: "He is junior to me in the company." / "They are senior to us by two years."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She will handling the baby as tenderly as possible.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She will handling the baby as tenderly as possible.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: will handle.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the verb 'handling' is incorrect as it should be in its base form 'handle' to match with the auxiliary verb 'will'.
  • The correct structure for future tense is 'will + base form of the verb'.
  • Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'handle' instead of 'handling'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: She will handle the baby as tenderly as possible.

Additional Information

  • When using modal verbs like 'will', 'shall', 'can', 'could', 'may', 'might', 'must', 'should', always use the base form of the main verb.
    • Example: She can handle the situation well.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They are the people which are looking to expand their horizons in the fast growing tourism industry.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They are the people which are looking to expand their horizons in the fast growing tourism industry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. 'who are looking to expand'.
Key Points
  • The sentence is referring to the group of people who have a certain aim to expand their horizons in the tourism industry. In English grammar, when referring to people, we use 'who' not 'which'.
  • The error in the sentence lies in the usage of the relative pronoun 'which' for referring to people. The correct relative pronoun to use for people is 'who'.
  • The verb form 'are looking to expand' correctly maintains agreement with the plural subject (the people).
Therefore, the corrected sentence should be "They are the people who are looking to expand their horizons in the fast growing tourism industry."
Additional Information
  • Option 1: 'which looked to expand' is incorrect because 'which' is not the correct relative pronoun to refer to people. Also, the use of past tense 'looked' is not consistent with the other verbs of the sentence that are in the present tense.
  • Option 2: 'who is looking to expand' is grammatically incorrect. 'Is looking' would be incorrect verb agreement for the plural subject 'people'.
  • Option 4: 'that are looked to expand' is grammatically incorrect. The verb phrase 'are looked to expand' doesn't make sense in the context of the sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. All the employees of the nationalized banks are in strike.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

All the employees of the nationalized banks are in strike.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- on.

Key Points​

  • ​There are some fixed prepositional phrases given below:
    • ​by the dint of, out of jealousy, on strike, by the dozen, owing to, on a trip, for a change, etc.
  • For example:
    • ​I went on a trip to Goa last month.
  • ​The phrase 'on strike' means (of employees) refuse to work as a form of organized protest, typically in an attempt to obtain a particular concession from their employer.
  • Thus the preposition 'on' will be the correct choice.
     

Correct Sentence: All the employees of the nationalized banks are on strike.

Additional Information

  • There are some verbs/nouns/adjectives which are followed by fixed preposition given below:
    • ​Exonerate from, refrain from, suspicious of, interested in, inured to, accused of, predilection for, respite from, vexed at, etc.
  • Example:
    • ​After spending some time on the island they became inured to the hardships.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Maheshwari is three years junior than me .

options.text: junior than any other to me

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. junior to me .

Key Points

  • The word "junior" is a comparative adjective that does not take the word "than" after it. Instead, it is followed by "to".
